sources.entry: psutil - A cross-platform process and system utilities module.

summary.one_liner: psutil is a cross-platform Python library for retrieving information about running processes and system utilization such as CPU, memory, disks, network, and sensors.
summary.what_it_does: It provides Python functions to query CPU usage and frequency, virtual and swap memory, disk partitions and usage, network I/O counters and connections, hardware temperature sensors, and battery status. It also exposes a Process class for inspecting and managing individual processes, including name, executable path, CPU and memory usage, open files, and network connections, plus process_iter for iterating over running processes. The README says it implements many functions of UNIX command-line tools such as ps, top, free, iotop, netstat, ifconfig, and lsof. Supported platforms listed are Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, Sun Solaris, and AIX. It is installed with pip.
use_cases: monitor system CPU and memory usage
inspect running processes and their resource use
list disk partitions and free space
check network connections and I/O counters per process
read hardware temperatures and battery status
limit or manage running processes from a script
notable: Cross-platform API covering Linux, Windows, macOS, BSD variants, Solaris, and AIX
Offers functionality similar to ps, top, free, iotop, netstat, ifconfig, and lsof from Python
Process class and process_iter for working with individual processes
Widely downloaded on PyPI according to the README
caveats: Platform-specific details are covered in a separate installation page, which the README links to but does not summarize
Some returned fields and behaviors vary by platform (the README links to an installation page for details)
